label: Warrant for the possible absence of a foundational simple being: PGP versus non-power accounts
summary: Issue #1887 tests 1-3, the assessment slice; tests 4-5 are a parallel formal slice. Note docs/notes/foundational-absence-warrant.md. Prose only: no statement, argument, result, definition, Lean or source-claim change. Analyst formulations, attribution deferred; every reference is marked read (URL, date, section) or navigation only. Fixed meanings: the candidate n is first (firstness 74eb9113, with B3 ee74c678) and simple in the route's sense (78246da5: no matter-form composition, esse = essence). 'Could be absent' means ContingentAt, the denial of NECESSARY_2 and S2 instantiated at n. Senses POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE (d25cee67) and POWER_OVER_ESSE (f5dda05f) are reused; an analyst change-power versus power-over-esse distinction is introduced with no corpus record. Test 1, evidence for the possibility itself. (a) Subtraction: SEP Nothingness s.7 (read) presents the contingency of each object as assumed, not argued. At n, S2 is the premise itself (6b12525b), so it fails criterion 3. (b) Conceivability: both sides grant the prima facie datum. ST I q.2 a.1 sed contra (read): the opposite of 'God is' can be mentally admitted. Necessary existence is equally not ruled out a priori. The unrestricted #248 StrongBridge applied to both is inconsistent on a Euclidean frame (an analyst derivation, requested as F1). An ideal positive conceiving would require knowing what n is; q.2 a.1 (read) locates the gap in 'because we do not know the essence of God'; the modal reading of this is an analyst extension. The epistemic half of the 'ignorance of essence' reply is neutral and independently supported: Arnauld's triangle case and the double-occurrence fallacy (Van Cleve s.3, read), and van Inwagen's reliability restriction (SEP Epistemology of Modality s.3, read as report). The specific difference from ordinary concreta: their conceivability verdicts are calibrated against observed generation and corruption, which n, without matter or received esse, lacks. So this objection also fails criterion 3. (c) Actual temporal absence is a genuine datum type, but no candidate with a beginning is on file. Symmetrically, PGP has no case datum. The actualist truthmaker demand separates PGP only from primitivism: essences ground absence for the essentialist, and actual objects do for Armstrong (as reported in SEP s.7). Powers-based modal epistemology (Pruss, read; Vetter per SEP s.6) gives agnosticism, not necessity, at n. An Oxford handout summarizing Vetter's ch.7 records that first entities come out necessary existents and that 'biting the bullet isn't so bad'; this is unchecked against the book. Test 2, the hybrid. ST I q.45 a.2 ad 2 and a.3 (read): creation is not change, because change needs a subject, and the subject of substantial change is matter. But q.9 a.2 (read) grounds creatures' possibility of existence in divine power, and q.104 a.3 ad 1 and ad 3 (read) grounds annihilation in a cessation of action, holding that non-existence has no direct cause. So 'existence is not a change' bounds passive-potency and change-power grounding, not power-grounding as such. The hybrid can keep POTENCY_1, motion as reduction and the act principle at subjectless cases (C2 law 10; bruteSimple). It must accept power-grounding for every generable and corruptible thing, since generation is a change of matter. Its boundary holds at subjectless coming-to-be and ceasing, where n falls, and fails at generation and corruption. It supplies no verdict at n: it explains only why the in-subject channel is empty, which PGP already uses. Test 3, costs. Primitivism delivers no verdict at n. Unrestricted combinatorialism's absence verdict rests on content (542c595e) that Hume's dictum does not independently motivate. Van Cleve (read, ss.2, 3, 10): Hume's derivation of the dictum is fallacious; the dictum's standalone intuition concerns dependence and admits a necessary-being exemption. A necessary n's trivial co-necessitation is not dependence. Existence-conditional essentialism cannot mark necessary existence (SEP Essential vs. Accidental Properties s.1.1, read) and makes esse = essence modally idle. It is the strongest standing rival; its general thesis that existence never belongs to an essence is unassessed as applied to an identity of esse and essence. Unconditional essentialism gives a second route to necessity, correlated with B6 through simplicity and not using PGP. Lowe's argument as reported in SEP s.7 yields only 'necessarily some contingent being'. PGP's 'unexplained lack of power' is no cost beyond its open premises: necessity is its default, as contingency is the rivals' default, and the lack is derived from passive-to-receptive with unreceivedness, correlation with B3 and firstness, and b62a64ab. Pruss's global-possibility problem (read) does not bear on n. Rejected: crediting either side with conceivability; counting disunity as a substantive cost of the hybrid; treating 'existence is not a change' as Aquinas's own boundary on power-grounding; attributing to Vetter what only the handout states. Expected frontier delta: none.
blocker: The decisive open question at n is whether existence can never belong to an essence (existence-conditional essentialism) as applied to an identity of esse and essence. The thesis is Kant-type, navigation only, and unassessed. Also open: correlation 9163c423 and b62a64ab; reading Vetter's own text; Pruss's joint-contingency premise against Van Cleve's 'all possibly to possibly all' point (test 5); positive conceivability of n's absence. Requested formal results F1-F5 (note s.8): conceivability parity on a Euclidean frame; the hybrid's restriction as a certified difference on CausalityFrame; an exposed lemma for PGP's lack of power at the first mover; existence-conditional versus unconditional essence on the B6 vocabulary; Hume's dictum with and without the necessary-being exemption.

current_assessment.scope: PGP 20d5fecd and the denial of S2 at the candidate necessary being (b19ffd92 via 6b12525b), at the possible absence of a foundational simple uncaused actual individual (route meanings of firstness 74eb9113 and simplicity 78246da5). The general-theory comparison of modal accounts beyond this node is not in scope.
current_assessment.assessment: At matching scope the possible absence of n has no discriminating positive warrant. Subtraction, conceivability and unrestricted recombination through Hume's dictum each fail at n for identified reasons, so as an objection to the route's necessity it fails criterion 3 of the substantive objection standard. One exception is unassessed: existence-conditional essentialism's thesis that existence never belongs to an essence. PGP likewise has no case datum. Its verdict at n rests on its general theory (motivations independent of theism) and on the open premises passive-to-receptive 16c760a3, correlation 9163c423 and b62a64ab; its 'lack of power' adds no further cost. Overall: PGP's verdict at n has qualified relative standing over the bare claim that n could be absent. It is not shown better warranted than existence-conditional essentialism, the strongest standing rival. The general-theory comparison remains unresolved. The hybrid is principled as a boundary for passive potency and change-powers and compatible with the First Way's act/potency commitments at subjectless cases, but supplies no verdict at n. Refines, without reversing, the C2 note's s.13 judgment. Nothing is established; no formal status changes.
current_assessment.next_test: Assess, from read sources, whether a thesis that existence never belongs to an essence applies to an identity of esse and essence rather than to conceptual containment. Its outcome decides whether existence-conditional essentialism is a substantive objection at n. In parallel, slice A's F1 (conceivability parity) and F4 (essence variants on the B6 vocabulary).
